claim: Moody's projects MWAA net revenue debt service coverage will fall from 1.63x in 2024 to approximately 1.3x over the next five years as new debt phases in.
source_title: MWAA goes to market
page_or_section: MWAA credit profile summary of Moody's May 2025 report
supporting_excerpt: Moody's notes that net revenue debt service cover ratio will decline to around 1.3x over the next five years compared to 1.63x in 2024.
caveat: Cited from Bond Buyer's summary of Moody's May 2025 report; the primary rating agency PDF should be reconciled before publication.

claim: MWAA plans to issue approximately $5.5 billion of new debt between 2025 and 2028, with adjusted debt per O&D enplanement projected to peak near $400 in 2028.
source_title: MWAA goes to market
supporting_excerpt: MWAA plans to issue approximately $5.5 billion of new debt between 2025 and 2028, which will result in adjusted debt per origin and destination enplanement peaking to around $400 in 2028.
units: USD billions of new debt; USD per O&D enplanement
caveat: Bond Buyer restatement of MWAA investor materials and Moody's/Fitch reports; verify against MWAA's Preliminary Official Statement.

claim: MWAA carries current airport system revenue bond ratings of Fitch AA-, Moody's Aa3, and S&P AA-, all stable outlook.
source_title: MWAA Credit Ratings
supporting_excerpt: Fitch rates MWAA's Airport System Revenue Bonds at AA- stable, and Moody's rates them Aa3 stable. Both agencies assign stable outlooks as of May 2025.
caveat: S&P rating cited from airport context packet consistent with mwaa.com investor page; if the airport site does not list S&P, restate from the rating agency directly.

claim: ACI-NA's 2025 Infrastructure Needs Study identifies $173.9 billion of five-year U.S. airport infrastructure needs, up 15.1% from the 2023 study.
source_title: New ACI-NA Reports Highlight Economic Impact and Growing Infrastructure Needs of U.S. Airports
supporting_excerpt: America's airports need at least $173.9 billion over the next five years to fund necessary infrastructure projects, up 15.1% from just two years ago.
units: USD billions over five years; percent change vs 2023 study
caveat: ACI-NA methodology relies on airport-reported CIPs and is directionally reliable but not audited.

claim: ACI-NA's 2025 study attributes $20.6 billion per year in capital needs to large-hub airports and $6 billion per year to medium hubs.
source_title: New ACI-NA Reports Highlight Economic Impact and Growing Infrastructure Needs of U.S. Airports
supporting_excerpt: Large hub airports account for 73.5% of all enplanements and total $20.6 billion in capital needs per year, while medium hub airports account for 16.7% of all enplanements and total $6 billion in capital needs per year.
caveat: Reported annualized from a five-year study; validate before quoting the per-year figure as measured spend.

claim: Announced large-hub airport capital programs total $130-140 billion through 2030.
source_title: Large-Hub Airport Capital Programs 2026
supporting_excerpt: Capital programs at all 31 FAA large-hub airports total $130-140 billion announced through 2030, anchored by megaprojects at JFK, SFO, DEN, DFW, and ORD.
caveat: Secondary consulting compilation; each underlying CIP should be verified airport-by-airport for citation-grade use.

claim: The Construction Industry Institute estimates direct rework at approximately 5% of total project cost on average, with a 2-20% range by project type.
source_title: Cost of Rework in Construction 2026
supporting_excerpt: The Construction Industry Institute estimates direct rework at an average of 5 percent of total project costs. However, the range is typically 2 to 20 percent depending on project type.
caveat: Third-party restatement of CII findings; the underlying CII RT-153 and related publications are the authoritative source and should be pulled if the number is used in a fact-checked article.

claim: Design-related errors account for 1-9% of total project cost in rework alone; up to 70% of construction rework traces to engineering and design errors.
source_title: Cost of Rework in Construction 2026
supporting_excerpt: Design-related errors are the single largest contributor to rework across project types, accounting for between 1 and 9 percent of total project cost in rework alone. Additionally, up to 70 percent of all rework in construction can be traced back to engineering and design-related errors.
units: percent of total project cost; percent of rework
denominator: total project cost; total rework volume
caveat: Same caveat as prior CII citation.

claim: SFO's Quiet Airport program reduced individual paging occurrences from 492 to 261 per day and cumulative announcement duration from 145 to 58 minutes per day, a 47% reduction in occurrences and a 60% reduction in duration, with overall onsite noise reduced by more than 40%.
source_title: San Francisco Airport Removed 90 Minutes of Daily Noise
supporting_excerpt: Individual paging from 492 to 261 individual occurrences, whose cumulative duration went down from 145 minutes to 58 minutes, equalling a 47% reduction in occurrences and a 60% cut to duration.
data_vintage: SFO Quiet Airport program results, program launched 2018
units: paging occurrences per day; minutes per day; percent reduction in occurrences and duration; percent reduction in onsite noise
caveat: Underlying measurement methodology is not verified in a primary source available in this pass; airport-context packet flags the same limitation.

claim: London City Airport has operated a silent terminal policy since 2008, with no flight or gate announcements since August 18, 2016, except for essential and emergency announcements.
source_title: Silent Airport Policy | London City Airport
supporting_excerpt: London City Airport implemented a 'silent terminal' policy from 2008... From August 18 (2016), the airport said no flight or gate announcements would be made, instead all information would be displayed on screens located throughout the lounge and restaurants.
caveat: Airport self-description; consistent with independent reporting.

claim: Schiphol describes itself as a Silent Airport with virtually no announcements and moves important flight information to FIDS and the app.
source_title: Schiphol | Flying for the deaf and blind
page_or_section: Silent airport section on Schiphol accessibility page
supporting_excerpt: All important information about your flight, such as gate changes, delays and cancellations, are shown on flight information screens, on this website and in the Schiphol app.
caveat: Airport self-description; the accessibility page is the operational statement rather than a Board-adopted design standard.

claim: Berlin Brandenburg Airport's initial budget of approximately €2.83 billion escalated to a final cost of €6.5-7.3 billion, opened nine years late in October 2020, with more than 100,000 construction defects catalogued by 2012.
source_title: Why Berlin Brandenburg Airport Took 14 Years
supporting_excerpt: An initial budget of €2.83 billion ballooned to a final cost of €6.5-7.3 billion... over 100,000 construction defects by 2012.
units: EUR billions; number of defects; years of delay
caveat: Restatement of a large secondary literature; individual figures are widely reported but the underlying German federal audit reports (Bundesrechnungshof) are the primary source for citation-grade use.

claim: Denver International Airport's automated baggage system escalated from a $193 million contract to more than $560 million in cost overruns, delayed opening by 16 months, and was ultimately largely abandoned.
source_title: The Failure of Denver International Airport's Automated Baggage System
supporting_excerpt: What began as a $193 million contract spiraled past $400 million... airport opened in February 1995, 16 months behind schedule with cost overruns estimated at $560 million, much of which was attributed to the baggage system.
caveat: Numbers vary across secondary sources; a GAO or City of Denver audit would be the authoritative citation.

claim: Heathrow Terminal 5 opened on 27 March 2008 at a cost of approximately £4.2 billion; over the following ten days approximately 42,000 bags failed to travel with their owners and more than 500 flights were cancelled following baggage-system failures.
source_title: Heathrow Terminal 5 - Wikipedia
supporting_excerpt: Over the following 10 days some 42,000 bags failed to travel with their owners, and over 500 flights were cancelled.
units: GBP billions; number of bags; number of flights cancelled
caveat: Wikipedia restates the widely-reported figures; House of Commons Transport Committee report (May 2008) is the authoritative primary source.

claim: Washington Dulles's AeroTrain system opened in January 2010 at a cost of approximately $1.5 billion using Mitsubishi Crystal Mover vehicles on a 3.78-mile alignment, and was built without a station at Concourse D.
source_title: Washington Dulles Details US$20 Billion-Plus Overhaul to Retire Mobile Lounges
supporting_excerpt: The airport's underground AeroTrain system opened in January 2010 at a cost of $1.5 billion, and was built by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries using Crystal Mover rubber-tired vehicles running a 3.78-mile underground track... the AeroTrain system was built without a station at Concourse D.
caveat: Trade press summary consistent with MWAA project history; MWAA historical CIP records would be primary.

claim: The IAD $20 billion-plus transformation budgets approximately $3.75 billion for AeroTrain extension and underground tunnel, with construction possibly beginning in spring 2027 and target schedule January 2028 through December 2033.
source_title: Washington Dulles Details US$20 Billion-Plus Overhaul to Retire Mobile Lounges
supporting_excerpt: The AeroTrain extension and underground tunnel are budgeted at roughly $3.75 billion. The target schedule for the AeroTrain and underground connector is January 2028-December 2033, and construction could begin in spring 2027.
caveat: Program figures announced in July 2026 rollout; verify against MWAA Board resolutions and program EA/EIS documentation.

claim: The 2025 Airline Use and Lease Agreement carried a capital construction program of approximately $9 billion at execution: approximately $6.99 billion at IAD and approximately $2.39 billion at DCA.
source_title: Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority Completes Negotiations for New Use and Lease Agreement with Airlines
page_or_section: Capital program summary in the press release
supporting_excerpt: The 15-year pact includes a new $9 billion capital construction program.
caveat: Program subsequently expanded per July 2026 announcement to $20B+ at IAD; the $6.99B and $2.39B splits are the amounts at execution.

claim: The New Terminal One at JFK is a $9.5 billion terminal within the Port Authority's approximately $19 billion JFK transformation, with total debt load exceeding $6 billion in bonds and opening delayed to at least November 2026.
source_title: Inside The $6 Billion Debt Clock Ticking On New York-JFK's Delayed New Terminal 1
supporting_excerpt: The project has a total debt load of $5.9 billion in bonds, with additional borrowings bringing the total to over $6 billion... expected to open in 2026. However, this opening date has been pushed back to November 2026 at the earliest.
airport_or_entity: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey / JFK NTO
caveat: Trade press summary; New Terminal One Green Bond OS and Port Authority filings are primary.

claim: MWAA current cost per enplanement is reported at approximately $12.77, low relative to ORD ($28.43 FY2024) and JFK (over $36).
source_title: Cost per Enplanement by Airport | CPE Data 2026
supporting_excerpt: Dulles currently has a CPE of $12.77, and ORD's FY2024 CPE was approximately $28.43, with projected CPE rising to approximately $40.06 by 2035.
caveat: Third-party compilation; FAA CATS filings and each airport's rates-and-charges resolution are primary.

claim: IEC 60268-16:2020 defines Speech Transmission Index measurement, and a STIPA value of 0.50 or above is typically required for voice alarm systems to comply with EN 54-16, BS 5839-8, and ISO 7240-19.
source_title: IEC 60268-16 Complete Guide: Speech Transmission Index (STI) Standard
supporting_excerpt: A STIPA value of 0.50 or above ('Fair') is typically required for voice alarm systems to comply with EN 54-16, BS 5839-8, and ISO 7240-19.
airport_or_entity: international standards regime for voice alarm systems
caveat: Primary standards are paywalled; the practical threshold cited is consistent with the underlying standards but the standards texts themselves should be used for authoritative citation.

claim: ACRP Research Report 175: Improving Intelligibility of Airport Terminal Public Address Systems provides design guidelines for PA speech intelligibility across passenger-processing environments and reports data on PA systems, terminal finishes, and background noise levels from participating airports.
source_title: ACRP Research Report 175: Improving Intelligibility of Airport Terminal Public Address Systems
supporting_excerpt: The guidelines include a summary of data on public address systems, terminal finishes and background noise levels in a variety of airport terminals, identification of acoustical shortcomings, and the results of impacts on existing public address systems.
caveat: The 2017 publication date pre-dates several new large-hub terminal projects; the guidance framework remains the U.S. reference document.

claim: The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 authorized 10 additional daily beyond-perimeter slot exemptions at DCA (5 nonstop round-trips), awarded in December 2024 to Alaska (SEA), American (SAN), Delta (SFO), Southwest (SAT), and United (LAS).
source_title: DCA Slot Expansion and MWAA Revenue Impact
supporting_excerpt: FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 authorized 10 additional daily beyond-perimeter slot exemptions at DCA (5 nonstop round-trips). DOT awarded these in December 2024 to Alaska (SEA), American (SAN), Delta (SFO), Southwest (SAT), and United (LAS).
units: daily slot exemptions; number of round-trips
caveat: Consulting restatement consistent with DOT public awards; the DOT slot allocation order is primary.

claim: The 1-10-100 cost-of-change heuristic in construction: an error costs 1x on paper, 10x in procurement, and 100x once built.
source_title: What are Change Orders in Construction?
supporting_excerpt: Following the 1-10-100 rule, an error that costs $1 to fix on paper costs $10 to fix during procurement and $100 once it's built.
caveat: Stylized heuristic, not a measured statistic; used in the brief as a framing device, not as a calculated result.

claim: MWAA system passenger traffic reached approximately 54 million in 2025 (29.01 million at IAD, up 6.4% YoY; 24.89 million at DCA, down 5.4% YoY), with IAD international traffic of 10.53 million (36%+ international share).
source_title: Airport Context Packet — MWAA (IAD and DCA)
supporting_excerpt: System combined: approximately 54 million passengers, a record year. IAD: 29.01 million passengers, up 6.4% YoY; 10.53 million international passengers.
units: millions of passengers; percent YoY change; percent international share
caveat: Context packet restatement; MWAA's 2025 traffic release and ACFR are primary.
